verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
David perceived that Yahweh had established him king over Israel; for his kingdom was exalted on high, for his people Israel’s sake.
David took more wives at Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went out against them.
Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the valley of Rephaim.
David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?” Yahweh said to him, “Go up; for I will deliver them into your hand.”
So they came up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal Perazim.
They left their gods there; and David gave a command, and they were burned with fire.
The Philistines made a another raid in the valley.
David inquired again of God; and God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle; for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did as God commanded him; and they attacked the army of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.
The fame of David went out into all lands; and Yahweh brought the fear of him on all nations.

footnotes.content: Hiram of Tyre sent cedar, masons, and carpenters—a gift that would have felt like God's own hand, turning away the hardship of building by force. David was surrounded by enemies, yet here came a foreign king with material blessing. Sometimes the Lord provides through the hands of those who see the worth of His anointed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David 'perceived'—he recognized in his bones that God had set him firm as king. Not through conquest alone, but through God's establishment. When we see God's hand at work, even in the smallest arrangement, it settles the heart in a way no earthly security can.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David took more wives and fathered more children—a sign of strength and dynasty. Yet this choice would later weigh heavy, as we see in Scripture's pattern of kings multiplying wives. Even God's anointed must learn that not every appetite honored is wisdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. Of these, Nathan and Solomon carry great weight in Scripture—Nathan the voice of correction in David's darkest hour, and Solomon who would build what David prepared. God often plants tomorrow's blessing in today's generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When enemies hear that God has anointed us, they rise against us—that's often how it goes. But notice David didn't hide or panic; he 'went out against them.' To serve the Lord is sometimes to stand firm where shadows gather, trusting His hand is already reaching into the conflict.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines raided the valley of Rephaim—a place where giants once walked, where David had already faced Goliath. Sometimes the Lord brings us back to old battlegrounds not to defeat us, but to show us how far His grace has carried us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David did not rush to war; he inquired of God first. 'Shall I go? Will you deliver them?' This is the simplicity that saves a king's life—to ask before acting, to wait for the word. God's answer came clear: 'Go up; I will deliver them into your hand.' The Lord does not leave His own to guess.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At Baal Perazim—'Lord of Breakthroughs'—David saw God act like waters breaking through a dam. Sometimes the Lord's deliverance is not slow or measured; it is sudden, powerful, and unmistakable. David named the place to remember. We, too, do well to remember where we saw God break through for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistine idols lay abandoned in defeat, and David's command was swift: burn them with fire. Not in anger, but in clarity—false gods have no place where the true God has shown His hand. To serve the Lord is sometimes to make clear where our allegiance rests.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines returned to raid again. One victory does not end all struggle. The Christian life knows this rhythm—we are not promised a single triumph that removes all trial, but the grace to meet each new trial as it comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David asked again; God gave new instruction: 'Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.' Not the same strategy twice. The Lord gives fresh wisdom for fresh trials, not a playbook we memorize and repeat. He knows what each moment requires.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When you hear the sound of marching in the mulberry trees—a physical sign, a divine signal. God chose to speak through creation itself, through wind and leaves, a whisper David would recognize. The Lord still speaks, often in the small stirrings we must listen for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David obeyed as God commanded, and they drove the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer—a sweep of deliverance across the land. Obedience to God's specific word, not our general instinct, is what opens the way to victory. The victory came because David listened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fame of David went out into all lands; Yahweh brought the fear of him on all nations. Readers today hear an echo: when we walk in obedience and the Lord's hand is upon us, our witness carries farther than we know—not through our strength, but through His. That same grace still travels on the wind.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
